activate.brief: Activates `area`, usually by activating the currently focused cell, however some subclasses which embed widgets in the area can also activate a widget if it currently has the focus.

cell, however some subclasses which embed widgets in the area
can also activate a widget if it currently has the focus.

activate_cell.brief: This is used by `GtkCellArea` subclasses when handling events to activate cells, the base `GtkCellArea` class activates cells for keyboard events for free in its own GtkCellArea->activate() implementation.
activate_cell.md:

to activate cells, the base `GtkCellArea` class activates cells
for keyboard events for free in its own GtkCellArea->activate()

add.brief: Adds `renderer` to `area` with the default child cell properties.
add.md: Adds `renderer` to `area` with the default child cell properties.

add_focus_sibling.brief: Adds `sibling` to `renderer`’s focusable area, focus will be drawn around `renderer` and all of its siblings if `renderer` can focus for a given row.
add_focus_sibling.md:
Adds `sibling` to `renderer`’s focusable area, focus will be drawn
around `renderer` and all of its siblings if `renderer` can
focus for a given row.

Events handled by focus siblings can also activate the given
focusable `renderer`.

add_with_properties.brief: Adds `renderer` to `area`, setting cell properties at the same time.
add_with_properties.md:
Adds `renderer` to `area`, setting cell properties at the same time.
See gtk_cell_area_add() and gtk_cell_area_cell_set() for more details.

attribute_connect.md:
Connects an `attribute` to apply values from `column` for the

attribute_disconnect.brief: Disconnects `attribute` for the `renderer` in `area` so that attribute will no longer be updated with values from the model.
attribute_disconnect.md:
Disconnects `attribute` for the `renderer` in `area` so that
attribute will no longer be updated with values from the
model.

attribute_get_column.brief: Returns the model column that an attribute has been mapped to, or -1 if the attribute is not mapped.
attribute_get_column.md:
Returns the model column that an attribute has been mapped to,
or -1 if the attribute is not mapped.

cell_get.md: Gets the values of one or more cell properties for `renderer` in `area`.

cell_get_property.md: Gets the value of a cell property for `renderer` in `area`.

cell_get_valist.brief: Gets the values of one or more cell properties for `renderer` in `area`.
cell_get_valist.md: Gets the values of one or more cell properties for `renderer` in `area`.

cell_set.brief: Sets one or more cell properties for `cell` in `area`.
cell_set.md: Sets one or more cell properties for `cell` in `area`.

cell_set_property.brief: Sets a cell property for `renderer` in `area`.
cell_set_property.md: Sets a cell property for `renderer` in `area`.

cell_set_valist.brief: Sets one or more cell properties for `renderer` in `area`.
cell_set_valist.md: Sets one or more cell properties for `renderer` in `area`.

copy_context.brief: This is sometimes needed for cases where rows need to share alignments in one orientation but may be separately grouped in the opposing orientation.
copy_context.md:
This is sometimes needed for cases where rows need to share
alignments in one orientation but may be separately grouped
in the opposing orientation.

For instance, `GtkIconView` creates all icons (rows) to have
the same width and the cells theirin to have the same
horizontal alignments. However each row of icons may have
a separate collective height. `GtkIconView` uses this to
request the heights of each row based on a context which
was already used to request all the row widths that are
to be displayed.

create_context.brief: Creates a `GtkCellArea`Context to be used with `area` for all purposes.
create_context.md:
Creates a `GtkCellArea`Context to be used with `area` for
all purposes. `GtkCellArea`Context stores geometry information
for rows for which it was operated on, it is important to use
the same context for the same row of data at all times (i.e.
one should render and handle events with the same `GtkCellArea`Context
which was used to request the size of those rows of data).

focus.brief: This should be called by the `area`’s owning layout widget when focus is to be passed to `area`, or moved within `area` for a given `direction` and row data.
focus.md:
This should be called by the `area`’s owning layout widget
when focus is to be passed to `area`, or moved within `area`
for a given `direction` and row data.

Implementing `GtkCellArea` classes should implement this
method to receive and navigate focus in its own way particular
to how it lays out cells.

foreach_alloc.brief: Calls `callback` for every `GtkCellRenderer` in `area` with the allocated rectangle inside `cell_area`.
foreach_alloc.md:
Calls `callback` for every `GtkCellRenderer` in `area` with the
allocated rectangle inside `cell_area`.

get_cell_allocation.brief: Derives the allocation of `renderer` inside `area` if `area` were to be rendered in `cell_area`.
get_cell_allocation.md:
Derives the allocation of `renderer` inside `area` if `area`
were to be rendered in `cell_area`.

get_cell_at_position.brief: Gets the `GtkCellRenderer` at `x` and `y` coordinates inside `area` and optionally returns the full cell allocation for it inside `cell_area`.
get_cell_at_position.md:
Gets the `GtkCellRenderer` at `x` and `y` coordinates inside `area` and optionally
returns the full cell allocation for it inside `cell_area`.

get_current_path_string.brief: Gets the current `GtkTreePath` string for the currently applied `GtkTreeIter`, this is implicitly updated when gtk_cell_area_apply_attributes() is called and can be used to interact with renderers from `GtkCellArea`...
get_current_path_string.md:
Gets the current `GtkTreePath` string for the currently
applied `GtkTreeIter`, this is implicitly updated when
gtk_cell_area_apply_attributes() is called and can be
used to interact with renderers from `GtkCellArea`
subclasses.

get_edit_widget.brief: Gets the `GtkCellEditable` widget currently used to edit the currently edited cell.
get_edit_widget.md:
Gets the `GtkCellEditable` widget currently used
to edit the currently edited cell.

get_edited_cell.brief: Gets the `GtkCellRenderer` in `area` that is currently being edited.
get_edited_cell.md:
Gets the `GtkCellRenderer` in `area` that is currently
being edited.

get_focus_cell.brief: Retrieves the currently focused cell for `area`
get_focus_cell.md: Retrieves the currently focused cell for `area`

get_focus_from_sibling.brief: Gets the `GtkCellRenderer` which is expected to be focusable for which `renderer` is, or may be a sibling.
get_focus_from_sibling.md:
Gets the `GtkCellRenderer` which is expected to be focusable
for which `renderer` is, or may be a sibling.

This is handy for `GtkCellArea` subclasses when handling events,
after determining the renderer at the event location it can
then chose to activate the focus cell for which the event
cell may have been a sibling.

get_focus_siblings.brief: Gets the focus sibling cell renderers for `renderer`.
get_focus_siblings.md: Gets the focus sibling cell renderers for `renderer`.

get_preferred_height.brief: Retrieves a cell area’s initial minimum and natural height.
get_preferred_height.md:
Retrieves a cell area’s initial minimum and natural height.

`area` will store some geometrical information in `context` along the way;
when requesting sizes over an arbitrary number of rows, it’s not important
to check the `minimum_height` and `natural_height` of this call but rather to
consult gtk_cell_area_context_get_preferred_height() after a series of
requests.

get_preferred_height_for_width.brief: Retrieves a cell area’s minimum and natural height if it would be given the specified `width`.
get_preferred_height_for_width.md:
Retrieves a cell area’s minimum and natural height if it would be given
the specified `width`.

`area` stores some geometrical information in `context` along the way
while calling gtk_cell_area_get_preferred_width(). It’s important to
perform a series of gtk_cell_area_get_preferred_width() requests with
`context` first and then call gtk_cell_area_get_preferred_height_for_width()
on each cell area individually to get the height for width of each
fully requested row.

If at some point, the width of a single row changes, it should be
requested with gtk_cell_area_get_preferred_width() again and then
the full width of the requested rows checked again with
gtk_cell_area_context_get_preferred_width().

get_preferred_width.brief: Retrieves a cell area’s initial minimum and natural width.
get_preferred_width.md:

get_request_mode.md:

or a width-for-height layout.

inner_cell_area.brief: This is a convenience function for `GtkCellArea` implementations to get the inner area where a given `GtkCellRenderer` will be rendered.
inner_cell_area.md:
This is a convenience function for `GtkCellArea` implementations
to get the inner area where a given `GtkCellRenderer` will be
rendered. It removes any padding previously added by gtk_cell_area_request_renderer().

is_activatable.brief: Returns whether the area can do anything when activated, after applying new attributes to `area`.
is_activatable.md:
Returns whether the area can do anything when activated,
after applying new attributes to `area`.

is_focus_sibling.brief: Returns whether `sibling` is one of `renderer`’s focus siblings (see gtk_cell_area_add_focus_sibling()).
is_focus_sibling.md:
Returns whether `sibling` is one of `renderer`’s focus siblings

remove_focus_sibling.brief: Removes `sibling` from `renderer`’s focus sibling list (see gtk_cell_area_add_focus_sibling()).
remove_focus_sibling.md:
Removes `sibling` from `renderer`’s focus sibling list
(see gtk_cell_area_add_focus_sibling()).

request_renderer.brief: This is a convenience function for `GtkCellArea` implementations to request size for cell renderers.
request_renderer.md:
This is a convenience function for `GtkCellArea` implementations
to request size for cell renderers. It’s important to use this
function to request size and then use gtk_cell_area_inner_cell_area()
at render and event time since this function will add padding
around the cell for focus painting.

set_focus_cell.brief: Explicitly sets the currently focused cell to `renderer`.
set_focus_cell.md:
Explicitly sets the currently focused cell to `renderer`.

This is generally called by implementations of
`GtkCellAreaClass.focus()` or `GtkCellAreaClass.event()`,
however it can also be used to implement functions such
as gtk_tree_view_set_cursor_on_cell().

snapshot.brief: Snapshots `area`’s cells according to `area`’s layout onto at the given coordinates.
snapshot.md:
Snapshots `area`’s cells according to `area`’s layout onto at
the given coordinates.

stop_editing.brief: Explicitly stops the editing of the currently edited cell.
stop_editing.md:
Explicitly stops the editing of the currently edited cell.

If `canceled` is `TRUE`, the currently edited cell renderer
will emit the ::editing-canceled signal, otherwise the
the ::editing-done signal will be emitted on the current
edit widget.

See gtk_cell_area_get_edited_cell() and gtk_cell_area_get_edit_widget().

edit-widget.brief: The widget currently editing the edited cell
edit-widget.md:
The widget currently editing the edited cell

This property is read-only and only changes as
a result of a call gtk_cell_area_activate_cell().

edited-cell.brief: The cell in the area that is currently edited
edited-cell.md:
The cell in the area that is currently edited

This property is read-only and only changes as
a result of a call gtk_cell_area_activate_cell().

focus-cell.brief: The cell in the area that currently has focus
focus-cell.md: The cell in the area that currently has focus

add-editable.brief: Indicates that editing has started on `renderer` and that `editable` should be added to the owning cell-layouting widget at `cell_area`.
add-editable.md:
Indicates that editing has started on `renderer` and that `editable`

apply-attributes.brief: This signal is emitted whenever applying attributes to `area` from `model`
apply-attributes.md: This signal is emitted whenever applying attributes to `area` from `model`

focus-changed.brief: Indicates that focus changed on this `area`.
focus-changed.md:
Indicates that focus changed on this `area`. This signal
is emitted either as a result of focus handling or event
handling.

It's possible that the signal is emitted even if the
currently focused renderer did not change, this is
because focus may change to the same renderer in the
same cell area for a different row of data.

remove-editable.brief: Indicates that editing finished on `renderer` and that `editable` should be removed from the owning cell-layouting widget.
remove-editable.md:
Indicates that editing finished on `renderer` and that `editable`
should be removed from the owning cell-layouting widget.
